units.title: Overnight interruptions: Gilliver feeder
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Customers in Gilliver, the harbour road and the Front Row cottages experienced three short interruptions overnight, at about 01:50, 02:30 and 03:15, followed by a longer loss of supply until 04:20 when engineers restored the feeder manually. Around 380 properties were affected. We apologise for the disruption and are investigating the cause.

units.title: Forecast: cloudy, mild, mist clearing
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound, issued 06:00 ST. Mist and low cloud around coasts at first, clearing slowly through the morning. Mostly cloudy and mild, dry. Wind southerly 3, veering southwesterly 4 later. Maximum 11 C. Tonight: cloudy, dry, a light southwesterly breeze. Mist unlikely. Minimum 7 C. High water at Gilliver 06:12 and 18:37.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op, update. Our initial investigation indicates that last night's interruptions on the Gilliver feeder were caused by salt-fog contamination of insulators following the recent storm, combined with heavy dew. This is a known effect on coastal lines. We are bringing forward insulator washing on the Gilliver and Brackwater coastal sections, which was planned for next week.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Insulator washing will take place on the Gilliver coastal section over the next three days, during daylight. Customers on the Gilliver, harbour road and Brackwater east lines should be aware that further short interruptions at night are possible until washing is complete. Please keep a torch handy and do not use candles near curtains.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. We are pleased to confirm that the additional 18:45 foot-passenger sailing from Port Ammet to Lisle and Gilliver will run from this evening, with a return from Gilliver at 19:35. The 20:15 continues as the last departure of the day. Night crossings remain reduced while the crew welfare review continues.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. The Lisle Spit buoy has been re-laid in its charted position and normal routeing into Lisle resumes from the 14:00 sailing. Thank you for your patience with the longer crossings this week.

units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. The Lisle Spit east cardinal buoy was re-laid this morning and its light is confirmed working, quick flashing three every ten seconds. The earlier notice is cancelled. Floating timber continues to be reported in the Gilliver channel. The small green rowing boat reported adrift has not been located.

units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Following inspection, the Gilliver sea wall has been found structurally sound. Repairs to lifted coping stones will start today and are expected to take four days. The harbour road remains single-lane at the wall during working hours and will be fully open overnight. The Front Row drain will be cleared this afternoon.

units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Garden waste collections in Tollinby and Brackwater will include storm debris for the next two weeks. Branches must be cut to under one metre and tied in bundles. Whole trees, stumps and fencing panels cannot be collected and should be taken to the Tollinby recycling centre, which is extending its opening hours to 19:00.

units.author: met
units.text: Evening forecast, 18:00 ST. Cloudy and dry overnight with a light southwesterly breeze. Relative humidity moderate, no mist or fog expected. Minimum 7 C. Tomorrow: cloudy start, brighter later, wind westerly 3. A small-craft advisory is not in force.

units.title: Unplanned outage: Gilliver and Brackwater east
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op, 22:10. We are aware of a loss of supply affecting around 600 properties in Gilliver, the harbour road and the Brackwater east line. Engineers are on their way. We believe this is related to the insulator contamination reported earlier today. Please treat all lines as live. We will post an update within the hour.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op, 23:10. Supply has been restored to Brackwater east. Gilliver and the harbour road remain off while engineers patrol the coastal section. We expect to restore supply by about 01:00. Customers who rely on powered medical equipment should call our priority line.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op, 00:50. Supply has been restored to all customers in Gilliver and on the harbour road. Patrolling engineers will remain on the coastal section overnight. Further short interruptions remain possible until insulator washing is complete. Thank you for your patience.

units.title: Carrow Point light on standby power
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. During the current mains interruption, Carrow Point light is operating normally on its standby supply. The Gilliver harbour entrance lights are also on battery. Mariners should note that shore lighting in Gilliver village and along the harbour road is out until further notice.

units.title: Gilliver: village hall open
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Gilliver village hall is open tonight as a warm space during the power cut, with a generator, hot drinks and phone charging, until supply is restored. Volunteers from the harbour and the chapel are on hand. Please check on elderly neighbours if it is safe to do so.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. A reminder that night crossings remain reduced: the last departure from Port Ammet is the 20:15 and there is no late return from Gilliver. Customers travelling to Gilliver this evening should note the village is subject to possible power interruptions; the terminal has its own standby lighting.

units.author: met
units.text: Tides and sea, Marrow Sound, next three days. Neap tides: high water Gilliver 06:12 and 18:37 today, 06:55 and 19:20 tomorrow. Tidal range around 2.1 m. Swell west 1 m, decreasing. Sea temperature 10 C. No warnings in force for coastal waters.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op, 01:40. A further brief interruption affected Gilliver for about four minutes at 01:30. Supply has restored automatically. Engineers on patrol are inspecting the coastal section. We understand how frustrating repeated interruptions are, and we thank customers for bearing with us while we complete the washing programme.

units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. Mariners are reminded that the Kittering Holm landing is a private working landing in regular use by supply craft. Small boats should keep clear of the landing approach and of log rafts or booms that may be moored nearby. Please report any unlit obstruction on channel 16.

units.title: Co-op blames storm salt for overnight power cuts
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Power Co-op has blamed salt left by this week's storm for a series of overnight power cuts in Gilliver, saying insulators on the coastal line had become coated with salt and then wetted by heavy dew. Around 380 properties lost power three times in the early hours before a longer cut that lasted until 04:20.

units.author: courier
units.text: The co-op said salt-fog contamination was 'a known effect on coastal lines after westerly gales' and that it had brought forward a programme of insulator washing on the Gilliver and Brackwater coastal sections. It warned that further short interruptions at night were possible until the work was complete.

units.author: courier
units.text: Residents of Front Row, still drying out after the sea came over the wall, said the cuts were the last thing they needed. 'You get the carpets up, you get the heater on, and then it goes off at two in the morning,' one said. 'Then on, then off. Like it couldn't decide.'

units.author: courier
units.text: A retired surveyor who runs a weather station near Carrow Point said his readings showed mist and very high humidity overnight, which he said was consistent with the co-op's explanation. 'Salt and dew on a calm night after a storm is textbook,' he said. 'I'd be more surprised if nothing had tripped.'

units.author: courier
units.text: The co-op said the Gilliver feeder had come through the storm itself without a single fault. Customers with concerns about frozen food can claim for spoiled goods under the co-op's guaranteed standards scheme if supply is off for more than twelve hours, which was not the case last night.

units.title: Live: power off again in Gilliver and Brackwater
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 21:45. We're getting reports from listeners in Gilliver that the power has gone off again, for the second night running. Sound Power Co-op hasn't put anything out yet. If you're in the village and it's safe, let us know what you're seeing. Please don't go out on the harbour road in the dark.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 22:12. The co-op confirms around 600 homes are off, in Gilliver, along the harbour road and on the Brackwater east line. Engineers are on their way. A listener on Front Row says it is completely dark along the front apart from the harbour entrance lights and 'a few windows with lamps in, the old way'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 22:40. The council has opened Gilliver village hall as a warm space with a generator. The Sound Lines terminal at Gilliver is on standby lighting. Our overnight producer, who lives up that way, tells us the Brackwater junction temporary traffic lights have finally changed colour: they're off.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:15. Power is back in Brackwater east, the co-op says. Gilliver and the harbour road are still off while engineers walk the coastal line. One question several of you have asked: the co-op's forecast partner said there would be no mist tonight. We've put that to the co-op and will share their answer when we get it.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 00:05. The co-op tells us salt contamination can cause faults on dry nights as well as damp ones if enough has built up, and that washing is the fix. A listener at Gilliver harbour says engineers with torches are walking the poles along the sea wall and 'looking up a lot'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 00:55. Power is back across Gilliver, a little before the co-op's estimate. We'll leave this page here for tonight. Thank you to everyone who called in, and to the volunteers at the village hall, who report that they went through four packets of biscuits and a box of candles they didn't need.

units.title: Dellow Court stairwell lights to be fixed today
units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates says the faulty timer relay blamed for weeks of stairwell blackouts at Dellow Court will be replaced today, ending a saga that tenants say has left floors six to eight in darkness most nights this month. A contractor is due on site this morning.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The managing agent said the replacement part had been 'subject to supplier delays' and thanked residents for their patience. The residents' association welcomed the news but said it would wait to see the lights stay on before thanking anyone.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Tenants have reported other problems during the blackout period, including noises on the stairs at night, which Kerrow Estates has previously attributed to the building's plant. The managing agent said it expected the new relay to 'resolve the issues residents have raised'.

units.title: Extra early-evening ferry to run from tonight
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines will run an extra 18:45 foot-passenger sailing from Port Ammet to Lisle and Gilliver from tonight, after filling a vacant deckhand post. The operator said the sailing was intended to ease crowding on the 20:15 while night crossings remain reduced.

units.author: courier
units.text: Commuters welcomed the change but said it did not help those finishing late shifts. The seafarers' branch confirmed that one deckhand had left the company this week for personal reasons and said it would not comment further. Sound Lines repeated that its welfare review would take 'weeks, not months'.

units.author: courier
units.text: Normal routeing into Lisle resumed this afternoon after the Coastguard's buoy tender re-laid the Lisle Spit marker, which had been dragged out of position in the storm. Crossings calling at Lisle had been taking about six minutes longer.

units.title: Remote crews: what does 'welfare' mean on an island job?
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: This week's decision by a Marrow Sound ferry operator to review the welfare of its night crews has prompted questions in the land trade about crews working remote sites. Island and estate jobs often involve small teams living on site for weeks, with limited transport and long winter nights.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Asked about its crew on the Kittering Holm clearance, Grieve Land Services said the welfare of remote crews was 'a priority' and that its site leads follow standard guidance on rest, lighting and communications. The firm said it would not discuss staffing on individual contracts.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: A former site lead who has worked island jobs said the basics had not changed in decades. 'Feed people properly, let them sleep, keep the camp lit and have a way off. Most of the trouble on remote jobs is tiredness and boredom,' he said. 'Most of it.'

units.author: courier
units.text: Update: council engineers have found the Gilliver sea wall structurally sound and repairs to the lifted coping stones began this morning. The harbour road will be fully open overnight while the work continues. The drain behind Front Row, blamed for flooding two cottages, was cleared of shingle and seaweed this afternoon.

units.title: Tower block lift replacement programme 'behind schedule'
units.author: weypost
units.text: A city-wide programme to replace ageing lifts in Weyhaven's tower blocks is running eighteen months behind schedule, a council report has found. Of the 23 blocks due to have new lifts by the end of this year, seven have been completed. Privately managed blocks are not included in the programme.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Tenants' groups said that when lifts fail, elderly residents can be confined to their flats for days. One residents' association secretary said older neighbours had begun 'planning their week around the lift', only going out when it was known to be working.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The council said the delay was caused by a shortage of specialist engineers and that it expected to complete the remaining blocks within two years. It has asked private landlords to share their own maintenance plans voluntarily.

units.title: Lisle Spit buoy back in place
units.author: soundfm
units.text: The Coastguard's buoy tender re-laid the Lisle Spit east cardinal buoy this morning, three days after it was dragged out of position by the storm. The tender's crew said the buoy had moved about eighty metres and its light had been damaged by debris.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Ferries can now take the normal route into Lisle again. A Lisle commuter who has complained to Sound FM every day this week about the extra six minutes said he was 'cautiously pleased' and would be timing tonight's crossing.

units.title: Brackwater thanks its storm volunteers
units.author: courier
units.text: Brackwater village hall committee has thanked the volunteers who kept the hall open as a warm space during the storm, when around 200 homes on the ridge road were without power for more than a day. More than ninety people used the hall, and volunteers served what one estimated was 'about a thousand cups of tea'.

units.author: courier
units.text: The committee said donations of flasks and a second kettle had made a real difference and asked residents to leave the hall's spare generator fuel where it was 'in case it's needed again soon'. The estate's ranger and his dog were thanked separately for checking on outlying cottages.

units.title: Co-op brings forward insulator washing
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Sound Power Co-op says crews will spend the next three days washing salt from insulators along the coastal lines serving Gilliver and Brackwater, a job originally planned for next week. Washing is done from the ground using high-pressure water, and some lanes may be briefly closed.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Asked by Sound FM whether the work would stop the night-time cuts, the co-op said it 'expected a significant improvement'. It said patrols had found salt deposits on several insulators near the Gilliver sea wall and no other faults so far.

units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: This is an automated message. The day-rate register for contract KH-30 has been updated with attendance to the end of the previous working day. Status: RECORDED. Next statement date: in four days. Reminder: the site timesheet window closes at 23:59 tonight. This mailbox is not monitored.

units.title: Leaver processed (ref GLS-LV-1801)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: This is an automated message. A leaver has been processed for contract KH-30. Final day rate has been calculated to the last recorded day of attendance. Status: LEAVER PROCESSED. The worker's site access has been closed in the register. No action is required by the site lead. Queries to Operations. Do not reply to this address.

units.title: Your winter catalogue is here!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Good morning! Our winter catalogue has landed: 64 pages of warm socks, thermos flasks, tarps, axe sheaths, hand warmers and our full lantern range. Inside: a voucher for 10% off your next order, a recipe for one-pot camp stew, and the answer to our autumn quiz (it was the heron). Remote sites can order by email for next-boat delivery. Happy browsing!

units.title: Mainland power cuts
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi, you may have heard there were power cuts in Gilliver overnight. The co-op says it's salt on the lines after the storm. Practically:
- the supply boat is unaffected
- the phone relay at Gilliver has battery backup, but signal may be patchy during a cut
- if you can't reach me, carry on as normal and I'll assume no news is good news
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Online talk
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a small thing. You may come across forum posts mentioning old Grieve jobs, sometimes by name. People who have worked for any firm for a long time have stories, and some of them grow. I'd rather we didn't get drawn into it, either on the forums or with the crew. The Holm is an ordinary clearance, just a big one. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, I've passed the site count to the client. I'm told they were pleased with the progress, which for them is quite a lot of feeling. Head office have asked me to say well done to you and the crew. Please don't let anyone ease off on the strength of it; there's still the second half to do. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the charter is loading at Gilliver now and should be alongside about 08:10 as planned. The skipper says the village had a rough night with the power. He'll want to be away again promptly, so it would help if someone is at the landing to take the lines. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Crew balance
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, I'm afraid I have to raise the crew balance again. Payroll's register still shows wages outstanding. I'm sure there's a reason, and I'd rather hear it from you than from head office. Remote crews talk about money more than anything else, and with the papers sniffing around I'd like this one settled quickly. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Tonight
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the Met Office says a mild, dry night. The co-op says there may be more cuts in Gilliver while they wash the lines. None of that touches you directly, but you'll see the village go dark if it happens. Nothing to worry about. Get some rest, all of you. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: sam
units.text: 6.45am, sitting in the car park. Mum's in, they've given her a gown that she says is 'an insult to the human form'. she's first on the list so it should be about nine. she said to tell you not to worry and that she has left instructions about the funeral just in case, which is a joke, I think. will email after. S x

units.author: sam
units.text: she's out and she's fine! surgeon says it went textbook, new hip is titanium and Mum says she's going to set off the airport scanners on purpose. she's woozy and asked a nurse whether you'd been fed. I said yes. have you been fed? she'll be in four days and then with me. the dog will have to learn manners. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: home now. visiting was a riot, she's already bossing the ward. driving back I had the radio on and Sound FM was going on about Gilliver being in the dark again. is that near you? it looked near you on the map. I know you'd tell me. I know you're fine. sorry, long day, I'm tired and it makes me silly. S x

units.author: sam
units.text: PS Bea says please can you send a photo of 'a real tree' for her costume research, and 'not a small one'. I said you'd try. also the dog has eaten one of Mum's get-well cards, the one from her bridge club, which honestly she won't miss. ok. bed. love you. S x

units.title: no joke today
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: heard Gilliver lost power again. that's the second night isn't it. you'll be able to see that from where you are, the whole village going out. funny thing to watch, a village going out. anyway. tell the crew a joke from me, any joke, I'm out of them. back on the road job tomorrow. H

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: sorry chief, that last one was a bit gloomy. it's the mud, it gets in your head. here's one for the crew: what's a tree's favourite drink? root beer. you can tell them it's from the best site lead they never met. might be quiet from me for a bit, the job's going to be long days. H

units.title: For your information
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello. A courtesy note rather than a question. Our trade colleagues asked Grieve this week about crew welfare on remote jobs, and Grieve said it was a priority. I'll be writing a short piece about the Holm landing, which the Coastguard mentioned in a notice today. I won't name you or anyone on the crew. If there's anything you would rather I didn't print, I would like to know. Nell

units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: I'm writing from my kitchen, by torchlight, as it happens: I live at the Gilliver end of the harbour road and we're in the second cut. From my window the only steady lights on the water are the harbour entrance and the Holm. I'm not sure why I'm telling you that. It seemed worth saying to someone. Nell

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, it's me, sorry. Nothing's wrong. I just read in the Post about the ferries and the power going in Gilliver, and Weyhaven had the lift article too, so it's all bad news this week. Tell Tomas I'm fine and I went to the cinema with my friend from Dellow Court and the film was terrible. Is he sleeping? Ana

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Sorry, one more, and then I'll leave you alone for a few days. My friend from Dellow says the lights in her stairwell were fixed today. She said it was the first night in weeks she didn't run up the stairs. I thought that was a nice thing to hear, so I'm passing it on. Ana

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Lantern week, day two! Thanks to everyone who ordered yesterday. Flash deal today only: buy any two Glowmaster lanterns and get a third at half price. Perfect for the porch, the shed, or a whole camp yard. Remember, a well-lit site is a happy site. Order by Friday for remote delivery. Stay bright!

units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.title: Lights Board survey of Kittering Holm (1953), part 3: attendance and recommendation
units.text: 6. Attendance. An unattended relay requires a visiting keeper at intervals of not more than seven days, with a hut for use in bad weather when the boat cannot return. Enquiries were made at Gilliver and Carrow Point as to men willing to undertake the duty, including overnight stays in the hut when required. No suitable man could be found at either place.

units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: 7. Recommendation. The site is technically suitable and the cost is within the Board's means. Nevertheless the undersigned recommends that the relay not proceed, for reasons of staffing, and that the Lisle channel be served instead by buoyage. The undersigned would be glad to discuss the staffing position with the Board in person rather than in this report. R. Talbot, CEng.

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Editor's note on part 3. 'No suitable man could be found' is consistent with the Board's national position in 1953-54: it was short of keepers and closing stations. Talbot's offer to discuss staffing 'in person' is ordinary civil-service caution about putting personnel matters on paper. I see nothing here that needs a footnote beyond that. Pell.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Editor's note, in reply. I agree it needs no footnote. I'd only add, for completeness, that the society holds no record of the in-person discussion Talbot offered, and the Board's minutes for that winter, which we checked in 1988, mention the Holm only as 'not proceeded with'. Whatever he wished to say, he said it aloud. Marsh.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Decr 14th. Clear and still. Felled 37. A good day and the men in better heart. In the evening Mr Coad read to us from the Psalms and Pascoe sang. Lamps in every window. Some talk in the long hut of the far lines and of who had been seen there, which Mr Coad stopped. Oil low, sent word for more by the next boat. Tally 2,412.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Decr 16th. Boat late, the oil not come. Lamps put out at ten by order to save what we have, all but the one in Mr Coad's hut. Trewin and his brother sat up by it until morning and were fit for nothing after. Felled 19. Roster 14. I have set down the oil as the most urgent want.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Middle watch. 00:00 wind SW 3, vis. good, no mist. 01:00 lamp trimmed, clockwork wound. 02:40 Remarks: three walkers on the shore road, standing, facing the village. Assistant keeper Penrose also saw them from the kitchen window and came up to the lamp room to say so. Hailed. No answer. 03:10 gone. 04:00 relieved. Penrose did not sleep.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Tape 15. Q: Your neighbour says the lamp is for the boats. A: [laughs] Well, she would. Her husband had a boat. No, it was for the dead. So they'd know the house still had the living in it and go on past. My granny said that. Q: Go on past to where? A: [long pause] Wherever they go. I don't hold with it myself. I keep one lit, mind.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Tape 16. Q: Did the lamps ever go out? A: In the war. Blackout. The warden came round and made us. My mother sat up all night by the window with it unlit in her lap, the matches by her. Every night for, oh, years. Q: Did anything happen? A: Nothing happened. That's what I'm telling you. Nothing happened, and she sat up anyway.

units.title: The Gilliver window lamp (custom)
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The Gilliver window lamp is a household custom of keeping a lamp lit in a front window through the night, recorded since at least the 1880s. Explanations collected by the 1976 oral history project differ: a guide for returning boats; a courtesy 'so they know the house is awake'; and, less often, a sign for the dead. The society takes no view. Observance declined after the 1960s but never ceased. [See tapes 14-16.]

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb 22. No fishing, gale. Mended nets in the shed all day with Tom. Mother angry with Tom for going down the slip last night after dark to see to the boat, says he should have left her, a boat can be fetched back and a man can't. Tom laughed but he did not go down tonight when the wind got up again. Lamp lit.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-2235 to LB-2237. Brackwater group session, night 4: three positions (dam path, reservoir road, pumping house), 22:00-03:50, synced. Outflow pipe events throughout; two percussive events at 02:12, dam path and reservoir road positions only, unattributed. LB-0412 (1974, reservoir dam works, donated by R. Ned) cross-referenced for comparison at the donor's request. Curator's note: six hours of owls, well recorded.

units.title: 1953: 'Gilliver Notes' on the Board men
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note: a reader asked whether the paper's village column mentioned the 1953 survey. It did, once, in a paragraph between a whist drive and a christening, reproduced here. 'The gentlemen from the Lights Board have been rowed across to the Holm each morning this fortnight by E. Rendle and brought back each afternoon in good time for their tea, which they take at the Anchor. They are said to be very good company and to tip handsomely.'
